questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: What is the East African Community?
questions.a: The East African Community is an inter-governmental organisation of East African countries that work together for their political, economic and social development.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Name the three countries that formed the EAC in 1967 and the leader of each.
questions.a: Uganda — Milton Obote; Kenya — Jomo Kenyatta; Tanzania — Julius Nyerere.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Where are the headquarters of the EAC?
questions.a: Arusha, in Tanzania.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Give any four reasons why the old East African Community collapsed.
questions.a: Any four of: differences in political ideologies; unequal sharing of benefits; personal differences between leaders; the 1971 coup in Uganda; lack of funds; nationalism and mistrust; each state starting its own services; border closures and war.
accepted: each state starting its own services

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: In which year was the EAC revived, and which two countries joined it in 2007?
questions.a: It was revived in 2001; Rwanda and Burundi joined in 2007.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Name any four organs of the East African Community.
questions.a: Any four of: the Summit, the Council of Ministers, the Co-ordination Committee, Sectoral Committees, the East African Court of Justice, the East African Legislative Assembly, the Secretariat.
accepted: the East African Court of Justice

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Give any four benefits of the present East African Community.
questions.a: Any four of: a large market; cheaper cross-border trade; free movement of people and goods; joint projects such as roads and railways; peace and security; employment; lower university fees for East Africans.
accepted: free movement of people and goods
joint projects such as roads and railways
lower university fees for East Africans

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Name any three symbols of the East African Community.
questions.a: Any three of: the EAC flag, the EAC emblem, the EAC anthem, the East African passport.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Give the capital city and currency of each of the five East African countries named in the syllabus.
questions.a: Uganda — Kampala, Uganda shilling; Kenya — Nairobi, Kenya shilling; Tanzania — Dodoma, Tanzanian shilling; Rwanda — Kigali, Rwandan franc; Burundi — Gitega, Burundian franc.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Why is East Africa called the cradle of mankind? Name one site where evidence was found.
questions.a: Because some of the oldest remains of early human beings have been found here. One site is Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania (also Koobi Fora in Kenya or Nsongezi in Uganda).

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Name the main ethnic groups of East Africa and give one tribe in each.
questions.a: Bantu — Baganda; River–Lake Nilotes — Acholi; Plain Nilotes — Karimojong; Highland Nilotes — Sebei; Cushites — Somali. (Any correct tribe for each group.)

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Give any four contributions of the Arabs and the missionaries to East Africa.
questions.a: Arabs: brought trade, Islam, Kiswahili and built coastal towns. Missionaries: brought Christianity, started schools and hospitals, and wrote down local languages. (Any four points in total.)

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Give the difference between a centralised and a decentralised society, with one example of each.
questions.a: A centralised society is ruled by one leader such as a king, for example Buganda under the Kabaka. A decentralised society has no single ruler and is led by clan elders, for example the Acholi or the Karimojong.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Give any five factors that influence where people settle in East Africa.
questions.a: Any five of: fertile soils, reliable rainfall, availability of water, security, good transport, employment, absence of pests and diseases, gentle relief, minerals, government policy.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Define population density. A district has 360,000 people and covers 4,500 km². Find its population density.
questions.a: Population density is the number of people living in one square kilometre. 360,000 ÷ 4,500 = 80 people per km².

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Give any four causes of rapid population growth in East Africa.
questions.a: Any four of: high birth rate, early marriages, polygamy, improved health services, falling death rate, better food supply, cultural and religious beliefs, low use of family planning, immigration.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Name two densely populated and two sparsely populated areas of East Africa, giving a reason for each.
questions.a: Dense: the Lake Victoria basin — fertile soils and reliable rainfall; the slopes of Mt Elgon or Kilimanjaro — fertile volcanic soils and relief rainfall. Sparse: Karamoja — too dry with little pasture and water; central Tanzania's miombo woodland — tsetse flies and poor soils.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Give any five problems caused by a high population density.
questions.a: Any five of: land shortage and conflicts; overcrowding and slums; unemployment; pressure on schools, hospitals and water; food shortage; poor sanitation and disease; soil exhaustion and erosion; destruction of forests and wetlands; traffic congestion; crime.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Suggest any four solutions to the problems of a high population.
questions.a: Any four of: family planning education and services; educating girls and discouraging early marriage; creating jobs; resettling people; building more social services; improving farming methods; developing rural areas; proper town planning.
accepted: educating girls and discouraging early marriage

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The East African Community
questions.q: Draw the map of East Africa and mark the five countries of the syllabus and their capital cities.
questions.a: Learner's map. Uganda — Kampala; Kenya — Nairobi; Tanzania — Dodoma; Rwanda — Kigali; Burundi — Gitega.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: What is a natural resource? Name any five natural resources of East Africa.
questions.a: A natural resource is a resource provided by nature. Any five of: land, water, minerals, vegetation, wildlife, climate, people.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Give any four uses of vegetation to the people of East Africa.
questions.a: Any four of: timber and poles, firewood and charcoal, medicine, pasture, raw materials for industry, protection of soil and water catchments, homes for wild animals, tourist attraction.
accepted: protection of soil and water catchments

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Name any four cash crops of East Africa and where each is grown.
questions.a: Any four, for example: coffee — Uganda and the slopes of Kilimanjaro; tea — Kericho in Kenya and Fort Portal in Uganda; cotton — eastern Uganda; sisal — Tanga in Tanzania; cloves — Zanzibar and Pemba; pyrethrum — the Kenya highlands.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Give any four factors that favour crop growing in East Africa.
questions.a: Any four of: fertile soils, reliable rainfall, suitable climate, enough land, available labour, markets and good transport.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: What is tourism? Name any four tourist attractions in East Africa.
questions.a: Tourism is travelling to visit places of interest for pleasure, study or rest. Attractions: Serengeti, Murchison Falls, Mt Kilimanjaro, the source of the Nile, the Indian Ocean beaches, the Kasubi Tombs (any four).

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Give any four importances of tourism to East Africa.
questions.a: Any four of: it earns foreign exchange; it creates employment; it earns government revenue; it provides a market for crafts and food; it leads to development of roads, hotels and airports; it promotes international friendship.
accepted: it provides a market for crafts and food
it leads to development of roads

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Give any three problems facing the tourism industry.
questions.a: Any three of: poaching, insecurity, poor roads to parks, high travel costs, destruction of habitats, shortage of skilled guides.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Name the mineral mined at each of these places: Kilembe, Mwadui, Lake Magadi, Geita.
questions.a: Kilembe — copper; Mwadui — diamonds; Lake Magadi — soda ash; Geita — gold.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Give the difference between traditional and modern mining.
questions.a: Traditional mining uses simple hand tools such as hoes, pans and baskets and digs shallow pits, while modern mining uses machines, deep shafts, drilling and dredging, and produces much larger amounts.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Name any two types of modern mining and give one example of each.
questions.a: Any two of: open cast — Hima limestone or Mwadui diamonds; shaft (underground) — Kilembe copper; drilling — oil in the Albertine Graben; dredging — minerals from river beds.
accepted: drilling — oil in the Albertine Graben

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Give any four problems facing the mining industry in East Africa.
questions.a: Any four of: shortage of capital, low technology and few skilled workers, remote deposits with poor roads, accidents, pollution, small scattered deposits, unstable world prices, smuggling.
accepted: low technology and few skilled workers

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Name any four lakes and any three rivers of East Africa.
questions.a: Lakes: Victoria, Tanganyika, Albert, Kyoga, Turkana, Kivu (any four). Rivers: Nile, Kagera, Tana, Rufiji, Pangani (any three).

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Give any five uses of water in East Africa.
questions.a: Any five of: drinking and domestic use, irrigation, hydro-electric power, fishing, transport, tourism and sport, industry, watering animals.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Name any three traditional and three modern methods of fishing.
questions.a: Traditional: hooks and lines, baskets and traps, spears, weirs (any three). Modern: trawling, purse seining, gill nets from motor boats, fish farming (any three).

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Give three traditional and two modern ways of preserving fish.
questions.a: Traditional: sun drying, smoking, salting. Modern: refrigeration and freezing, canning.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Give any five importances of fishing to the people of East Africa.
questions.a: Any five of: it provides food rich in protein; employment; income for families; foreign exchange from exports; raw materials for industries; government revenue; growth of landing sites and towns.
accepted: it provides food rich in protein
growth of landing sites and towns

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Give any five problems facing the fishing industry.
questions.a: Any five of: over-fishing; use of undersized nets; poison and explosives; water hyacinth; pollution; poor preservation and transport; lack of capital; accidents on the lakes; insecurity; low prices from middlemen.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Suggest any five solutions to the problems of the fishing industry.
questions.a: Any five of: enforce laws on net sizes and closed seasons; ban poison and explosives; encourage fish farming; remove water hyacinth; build cold rooms and improve roads; give loans and training; provide life jackets; form cooperatives; patrol the lakes.
accepted: enforce laws on net sizes and closed seasons
build cold rooms and improve roads

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Why are minerals said to be a source of income to a country?
questions.a: Because minerals are sold both at home and abroad, earning foreign exchange; they provide employment and wages; the government collects taxes and royalties from mining companies; and they supply raw materials for industries, which creates more income and jobs.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Major Resources of East Africa
questions.q: Draw the map of East Africa and mark on it Lake Victoria, the River Nile and Kilembe.
questions.a: Learner's map. Lake Victoria in the middle of the region, the River Nile flowing north from Jinja, and Kilembe in western Uganda near the Rwenzori.

topics.title: Transport and Communication in East Africa

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Define communication and transport.
questions.a: Communication is the sending and receiving of messages, information or ideas. Transport is the movement of people and goods from one place to another.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Name any five traditional means of communication.
questions.a: Any five of: drums, horns, trumpets, whistles, smoke signals, specialised messengers, alarms and screaming, rock pictures and signs, town criers.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Give any four challenges of traditional communication.
questions.a: Any four of: messages could be misunderstood; they covered short distances; they were slow; one needed to know the code; the enemy could also hear them; no record was kept; messengers faced danger.
accepted: one needed to know the code
the enemy could also hear them

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Name any six modern means of communication.
questions.a: Any six of: letters and telegrams through the post office, telephones (mobile and landline), radio calls, radio, television, newspapers, notice boards and billboards, the internet, e-mail, fax.
accepted: letters and telegrams through the post office

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Give any four advantages of modern communication.
questions.a: Any four of: it is very fast; it covers long distances; records can be kept; it carries pictures and detail; it reaches many people at once; it supports business and creates jobs.
accepted: it reaches many people at once
it supports business and creates jobs

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Give any four challenges facing modern communication in East Africa.
questions.a: Any four of: high cost of phones, airtime and data; no electricity or network in rural areas; illiteracy; language barriers; poor roads delaying post; breakdowns and power cuts; fraud and con artists; false information.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Suggest any four solutions to the challenges of modern communication.
questions.a: Any four of: extend electricity and network masts to rural areas; promote adult literacy and ICT in schools; reduce the cost of airtime and data; improve roads; use solar power; enforce laws against fraud; broadcast in local languages.
accepted: extend electricity and network masts to rural areas
promote adult literacy and ICT in schools
reduce the cost of airtime and data

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Name any four traditional means of transport.
questions.a: Any four of: walking on foot, head porterage, stretchers, donkeys, camels, oxen and ox carts, canoes, rafts, dhows.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Give any three challenges of traditional transport.
questions.a: Any three of: it was slow; only small loads could be carried; it was tiring; it was dangerous because of wild animals, robbers and drowning; goods went bad on the way.
accepted: only small loads could be carried
it was dangerous because of wild animals
goods went bad on the way

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Name the five modern forms of transport used in East Africa.
questions.a: Road, railway, air, water and pipeline.
accepted: Road, railway, air, water and pipeline.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Give two advantages and two disadvantages of road transport.
questions.a: Advantages: it reaches almost everywhere, door to door, and it is flexible and cheap for short distances. Disadvantages: accidents and traffic jams; roads are damaged by rain and it is costly for heavy loads over long distances.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Give two advantages and two disadvantages of air transport.
questions.a: Advantages: it is the fastest and it is good for perishable goods and remote places. Disadvantages: it is the most expensive and it carries only small loads (it is also affected by bad weather).

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Why is water transport preferred for very heavy goods?
questions.a: Because it is the cheapest way of moving very heavy and bulky goods over long distances, and ships can carry huge amounts at once, even though it is slow.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Name the two main sea ports used by the East African countries.
questions.a: Mombasa in Kenya and Dar es Salaam in Tanzania.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Name the three landlocked countries of East Africa.
questions.a: Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Which means of transport is used to carry oil over long distances, and give one of its advantages?
questions.a: A pipeline. It carries oil continuously and safely, with a low running cost and no traffic jams or accidents on the road.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Give any five importances of transport and communication in East Africa.
questions.a: Any five of: carrying goods to markets and raw materials to industries; taking people to school, work and hospital; promoting trade; creating employment; spreading news and knowledge; helping government services and security; promoting unity and tourism.
accepted: carrying goods to markets and raw materials to industries

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Give any five problems facing transport in East Africa.
questions.a: Any five of: poor roads; traffic jams; accidents; high fuel costs; old vehicles and trains; insecurity; difficult physical features such as swamps and mountains; being landlocked; shortage of funds.
accepted: difficult physical features such as swamps and mountains

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Suggest any five solutions to the transport problems of East Africa.
questions.a: Any five of: tarmac and repair roads; widen roads and build by-passes; enforce traffic laws and vehicle inspection; rebuild and extend the railway; improve lake ports and ferries; train drivers; strengthen EAC cooperation at borders; build pipelines; attract investment.
accepted: enforce traffic laws and vehicle inspection

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Transport and Communication in East Africa
questions.q: Draw the map of East Africa and mark on it Mombasa, Dar es Salaam and Entebbe.
questions.a: Learner's map. Mombasa and Dar es Salaam on the Indian Ocean coast, and Entebbe on the northern shore of Lake Victoria in Uganda.

topics.title: The Road to Independence in East Africa

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Who is an explorer? Name any four explorers who came to East Africa.
questions.a: An explorer is a person who travels to an unknown place in order to find out about it. Any four of: Speke, Grant, Burton, Baker, Livingstone, Stanley, Krapf, Rebmann.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Which two explorers reached the source of the Nile, and in which year?
questions.a: John Hanning Speke and James Grant, in 1862.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Give any four reasons why the explorers came to East Africa.
questions.a: Any four of: to find the source of the Nile; to map the interior; to look for raw materials and markets; to spread Christianity; to help stop the slave trade; for adventure and fame.
accepted: to find the source of the Nile
to look for raw materials and markets
to help stop the slave trade

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Give any four challenges the explorers faced.
questions.a: Any four of: tropical diseases; hostile people; wild animals; thick forests, swamps and mountains; language barriers; shortage of food and clean water; desertion by porters.
accepted: shortage of food and clean water

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Name the colonial master of each: Uganda, Kenya, Tanganyika (after 1919), Rwanda and Burundi.
questions.a: Uganda — Britain; Kenya — Britain; Tanganyika after 1919 — Britain (Germany before); Rwanda and Burundi — Belgium (Germany before).

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Give the difference between a colony and a protectorate.
questions.a: A colony is ruled directly by the foreign power, whose officers govern it; a protectorate is protected and controlled by the foreign power but is governed largely through its own traditional rulers.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: What is indirect rule, and which colonial power used it?
questions.a: Indirect rule is governing a colony through the existing African chiefs and traditional systems. It was used by Britain.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Give any four positive and four negative effects of colonial rule in East Africa.
questions.a: Positive: roads and railways were built; schools and hospitals were started; new cash crops were introduced; the slave trade was stopped (any four). Negative: Africans lost independence and land; forced labour and heavy taxes; African culture was weakened; traditional rulers lost power; raw materials were exploited (any four).

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: What was the Mau Mau, and in which country did it take place?
questions.a: The Mau Mau was an armed struggle (1952–1960) for land and freedom. It took place in Kenya.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Give the date of independence of Uganda, Kenya, Tanganyika, Rwanda and Burundi.
questions.a: Uganda — 9 October 1962; Kenya — 12 December 1963; Tanganyika — 9 December 1961; Rwanda — 1 July 1962; Burundi — 1 July 1962.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Name the first leader of each East African country at independence.
questions.a: Uganda — Milton Obote (Prime Minister), with Sir Edward Mutesa II as first President; Kenya — Jomo Kenyatta; Tanganyika — Julius Nyerere; Rwanda — Grégoire Kayibanda; Burundi — Mwami Mwambutsa IV.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: How was Tanzania formed?
questions.a: Tanzania was formed on 26 April 1964 by the union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Give any four methods used by East Africans in the struggle for independence.
questions.a: Any four of: forming political parties; forming trade unions; strikes and boycotts; petitions and delegations; newspapers and rallies; armed struggle; taking part in elections.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Give any five challenges faced by East African countries after independence.
questions.a: Any five of: military coups; dictatorship and abuse of human rights; civil wars; the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda; tribalism and nepotism; corruption; poverty and unemployment; refugees; heavy foreign debts.
accepted: dictatorship and abuse of human rights
the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Define democracy and give any four features of a democratic country.
questions.a: Democracy is government of the people, by the people and for the people. Features: free and fair elections; freedom of speech and the press; respect for human rights; the rule of law; accountable leaders (any four).

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Give four ways in which a person can become a citizen.
questions.a: By birth, by descent, by registration and by naturalisation.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Give any five rights and five responsibilities of a citizen.
questions.a: Rights: life, education, property, freedom of speech and worship, health care, a fair trial, voting, movement (any five). Responsibilities: obeying the law, paying taxes, protecting public property and the environment, voting, respecting others' rights, keeping peace, reporting crime (any five).

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Outline the steps of the electoral process.
questions.a: Voter registration → nomination of candidates → campaigning → polling day with a secret ballot → counting the votes → declaring the results → swearing in of the winner (with complaints going to the courts).

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Give any five challenges of the electoral process and three solutions.
questions.a: Challenges: rigging; bribery of voters; violence and intimidation; illiteracy; late delivery of materials; low turnout; errors in the register (any five). Solutions: an independent Electoral Commission with a clean register; civic and voter education; observers, agents and police at polling stations, with rigging and bribery punished (any three).

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: The Road to Independence in East Africa
questions.q: Draw the map of East Africa and write in each country its year of independence.
questions.a: Learner's map. Tanganyika 1961, Uganda 1962, Rwanda 1962, Burundi 1962, Kenya 1963.

topics.title: Responsible Living in the East African Environment

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Define the environment and environmental conservation.
questions.a: The environment is everything that surrounds us — land, water, air, plants, animals and people. Conservation is protecting and looking after natural resources so that they are not used up or destroyed.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Give the difference between afforestation and reafforestation.
questions.a: Afforestation is planting trees where there were none before, while reafforestation is replanting trees in an area where trees were cut down.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Name any five proper methods of farming that protect the soil.
questions.a: Any five of: crop rotation, mulching, terracing, contour ploughing, strip cropping, applying manure, controlled grazing, fallowing, planting cover crops.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Give any four alternative sources of energy that save trees.
questions.a: Any four of: solar energy, biogas, hydro-electric power, wind energy, energy-saving stoves, briquettes.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: What is waste management?
questions.a: Waste management is the collecting, sorting, treating and disposing of rubbish and other waste in a safe way.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Give the difference between biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste, with two examples of each.
questions.a: Biodegradable waste rots naturally, for example food remains and leaves. Non-biodegradable waste does not rot, for example polythene bags and glass.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Explain the three Rs of waste management.
questions.a: Reduce — use less of what becomes rubbish; Reuse — use items such as bottles and sacks again; Recycle — make waste into new useful things such as plastic basins from old plastic.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Give any four dangers of poor waste disposal.
questions.a: Any four of: blocked drainage and flooding; diseases such as cholera and malaria; pollution of soil, water and air; bad smells; injuries from broken glass; death of animals that swallow polythene; ugly surroundings.
accepted: diseases such as cholera and malaria
death of animals that swallow polythene

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: What does NEMA stand for, and in which year did it start work?
questions.a: National Environment Management Authority; it started work in 1995.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: State any five functions of NEMA.
questions.a: Any five of: coordinating environmental activities; making and enforcing standards; carrying out environmental impact assessments; monitoring pollution; protecting wetlands and forests; educating the public; advising government; punishing offenders.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Define climate change and give any four of its causes.
questions.a: Climate change is a long-term change in the normal climate of an area. Causes: deforestation, bush burning, swamp reclamation, smoke from factories and vehicles, overgrazing (any four).

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Give any four effects of climate change in East Africa.
questions.a: Any four of: unreliable rainfall; longer droughts; heavier storms and floods; melting of ice on Kilimanjaro and Rwenzori; drying lakes and rivers; famine; more crop pests.
accepted: melting of ice on Kilimanjaro and Rwenzori

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Give any five consequences of irresponsible living in the environment.
questions.a: Any five of: floods, landslides, desertification, pollution of land, water and air, diseases, resource depletion, pressure from a very fast-growing population, loss of wildlife, soil erosion, silting of lakes.
accepted: pressure from a very fast-growing population

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Why is it dangerous to build houses in a wetland?
questions.a: Because a wetland holds water like a sponge. When it is filled in and built on, the water has nowhere to go, so the area floods; the houses stand on weak, waterlogged ground; the wetland can no longer filter water or provide fish, papyrus and water for the community.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Give any two causes of landslides and two ways of preventing them.
questions.a: Causes: cutting trees and farming on steep slopes; heavy prolonged rain on loose soil (also digging and building on steep ground). Prevention: plant trees and grass on steep slopes; make terraces and dig contour trenches; avoid cultivating and settling on very steep land; resettle people from dangerous slopes.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: What is desertification, and which parts of East Africa are most affected?
questions.a: Desertification is the spread of desert conditions into land that was not desert before. It affects Karamoja in Uganda and northern Kenya most (also parts of central Tanzania).

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Give any six solutions to the environmental problems of East Africa.
questions.a: Any six of: afforestation and reafforestation; energy-saving stoves, biogas and solar; proper farming methods; protecting wetlands and river banks; proper waste management; treating sewage and factory waste; enforcing laws through NEMA; environmental education; family planning education; resettling people from dangerous areas; joint EAC action.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Give any four things a P.6 learner can do to protect the environment.
questions.a: Any four of: plant and water a tree; use both sides of paper; pick up and sort rubbish; never burn polythene; use a latrine; save water and switch off lights; join the school environment club; teach others.
accepted: save water and switch off lights

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Why should the East African countries work together on environmental issues?
questions.a: Because the environment is shared — Lake Victoria, the River Nile, the air and the migrating wildlife cross borders. Pollution or deforestation in one country affects the others, so laws, research and clean-up efforts work best when the countries act together through the EAC.

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Responsible Living in the East African Environment
questions.q: Draw a poster message of not more than ten words encouraging people to protect the environment.
questions.a: Learner's poster. For example: "Plant a tree today, save your tomorrow."
